name: How can I tell if a remodeled shower is properly waterproofed before the tile goes in?

mainEntity.name: How can I tell if a remodeled shower is properly waterproofed before the tile goes in?

acceptedAnswer.text: Waterproofing is a system, not just a coating applied to visible tile. The shower area needs compatible waterproof layers, properly treated seams and penetrations, a correctly sloped base, and a drain connection that prevents water from reaching framing and adjacent finishes. Elite Remodeling & Design can account for waterproofing during the construction planning stage rather than treating it as a final cosmetic step. Key factors include: - Shower pan or base condition - Wall transitions and corners - Valve and pipe penetrations - Threshold, niche, and bench details. Ask what waterproofing system will be used and how it is inspected before tile covers it. Photographing concealed work can also preserve a useful project record.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ask to review the waterproofing system before tile covers it, including the shower base, seams, corners, niches, penetrations, slope, and drain connection. Waterproofing should be treated as a coordinated assembly, not a last-minute surface coating.
